assessment_memory_pauses.outcome: The assessment closed between episodes. A fresh process passed with 2,058,616,832 available physical bytes and continued from the same ledger without rerunning completed episodes.
A second between-episode pause preserved 58 results. A new process passed the startup gate with approximately 1.07 GB of available physical memory and resumed the pending case ordering.

The third pause occurred because the process-start memory threshold was also applied after Torch and all actor classes were resident. Subsequent starts retain the 768 MiB process-start floor. A single additional engine inside an existing evaluator requires 512 MiB physical and 1 GB commit headroom. The running stop checks use a 256 MiB physical floor and retain all C: limits.

diagnosis: The original-baseline whole-drive decline exceeded the hard cap even with no DoomRay process active. C: still had about 29 GB of absolute free space. Docker/WSL virtual disks were active and Windows memory pressure was high. Neither activity is sufficient to attribute the historical free-space decline to a specific service or to DoomRay, because comparable allocation data at the original baseline is unavailable. The project runtime and new artifacts remain on D:.
recovery: No positively identified disposable project-generated C: files were found to safely recover enough space. No files were removed or relocated. No system or pagefile settings were changed. The user explicitly approved increasing the task-specific C: decline cap without changing the original baseline or reserve.
gate: Do not start any simulator, actor, or examination workload until at least 500,000,000 bytes remain under the authorized 7 GB C: decline cap and sufficient memory and absolute space are confirmed.
